account: It is day 1 at six in the morning, and I have just woken at home. I have not yet observed today's town activity. Yesterday the unusual matter was how ordinary delivery questions became rumours: my neighbour said they personally heard Freight offer wheat collection and bread delivery, while others turned this into talk of bridge or port changes and decorations for a celebration. The neighbour named Townsfolk 02 as a source of reports without firsthand details. I have no evidence of a planned celebration or infrastructure change. The builder reported no confirmed damage at the bridge, ferry, or warehouse. I authorized neither repairs nor paid inspections. These may simply be rumours arising from delivery arrangements; I do not know anyone's further purpose. Yesterday I verified 128 emeralds in the treasury, removed none, and learned from the secretary that the accounts minutes and balance addendum were filed, with income and expenses still unverified. No new correspondence or meeting requests had reached the secretary. Today my remembered schedule is office at eight, a routine mill grain inspection at ten, lunch at home, council letters at thirteen, tea at the neighbour's east-bank cottage at fifteen, office at sixteen thirty, and home at nineteen. I asked the secretary to request grain stock and delivery records for the mill inspection, explicitly without spending authorization. I should read the appointment book in the office this morning; the secretary last said they held it.
